editorial.headline: Inland Port Operations, and Bali’s Clearer PMA Line
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the working infrastructure of inland-water ports—and remains nationally open to full foreign ownership, without a Bali PMA moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Indonesia’s inland-water transport network depends on more than vessels. This activity covers the operation of ports serving rivers, canals, lakes, swamps and other inland waters in connection with passenger, animal or goods transport. Nationally, it is open to foreign investment with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In Bali, the record does not mark the activity as blocked for PMA registration under the province-wide moratorium.

The practical subject here is port operation: running terminal facilities such as ports and docks; operating river and lake navigation; and providing the services that make a vessel’s arrival, movement and departure work in practice. That includes sailing and berthing activities, mooring, pilotage and towing. The scope also includes inspecting cargo in freight and/or containers using ionising-radiation sources. It is therefore an operational category for the inland-water port environment itself, rather than a catch-all description for every service that may occur around a waterfront.

The activity is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the Bali reading turns on the risk signal recorded at the Besar scale: OSS classifies it as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. Since this activity carries the higher risk classification at that scale, the record identifies it as not blocked by that moratorium.

The national and Bali positions should be read together, not as competing answers. At national level, foreign ownership may reach 100% under the cited PMA basis. In Bali, the relevant question is not whether foreign ownership is nationally available, but whether the activity falls within the province’s blocked risk bands. On this record, it does not. For an operator considering an inland-water port business, that produces a straightforward conclusion: full foreign ownership is nationally available, and Bali’s PMA moratorium does not itself bar registration of this activity today.
